intro.data: A payment is either a card or cash. Build ONE handler that copes with both: charge the card, log the cash. One handler covers both cases correctly; the other mishandles the card. Pick the genuine case-split.
intro.alchemy: A reagent is either acid or base. Build ONE handler that neutralizes both. One covers both cases; the other mishandles one. Pick the genuine case-split.
intro.spellcraft: A charm is either ward or hex. Build ONE handler that resolves both. One covers both; the other mishandles one. Pick the genuine case-split.
intro.abstract: Build [f,g] : A+B→Y that handles both injected cases correctly.

goal.data: One handler that turns a card payment into its receipt AND a cash payment into its receipt.
goal.alchemy: One handler that neutralizes both acid and base correctly.
goal.spellcraft: One handler that resolves both ward and hex correctly.
goal.abstract: Handle both cases of A+B to Y.

description.data: a payment — either a card or cash
description.alchemy: a reagent — either one kind or the other
description.spellcraft: a charm — either one kind or the other
description.abstract: the coproduct A+B (one case OR the other)

description.data: one handler that copes with BOTH cases — charges a card, logs cash
description.alchemy: one process that copes with BOTH cases
description.spellcraft: one working that copes with BOTH cases

description.data: same type, but botches the card case
description.alchemy: same type, but botches one case
description.spellcraft: same type, but botches one case

afterSuccess.data: Your handler turned a card into its receipt AND a cash payment into its receipt — both cases, one machine. The look-alike mishandled the card. A coproduct's case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Your handler neutralized both acid and base. The look-alike botched one. A case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Your handler resolved both ward and hex. The look-alike botched one. A case-split must cover every injection.
afterSuccess.abstract: Both injected cases handled: [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g. The look-alike failed one case.

reveal.summary: The coproduct is the dual of the product: for f : A→Y and g : B→Y there is a unique [f,g] : A+B→Y with [f,g]∘ι₁ = f and [f,g]∘ι₂ = g — it must handle BOTH cases.
reveal.moreFormal: Reverse every arrow in the product's universal property and you get the coproduct's. Products are 'and'; coproducts are 'or'.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: match (p) { case Card: f(p); case Cash: g(p) } — miss a case and it's wrong.
